newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia has another national car in design stage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia has another national car in design stage.

text.p: Indonesia's national car controversy took on an added dimension on Tuesday when Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie said one of his departments would press ahead with its own car design.
Habibie told a parliamentary commission hearing in a written report that the Maleo vehicle project under the Strategic Industry Body (BPIS) had entered the second stage of development.
"Up until now we have already finished the first phase of the design development by BPIS in cooperation with Millard Design Australia, an automotive engineering design company," the report said.

"The activities in phase two (the detailed engineering design and testing) will be finished at the end of 1997," Habibie said. "A large part of these activities will involve technical experts from Indonesia's strategic industries."
The official Antara news agency later quoted Habibie as telling the commission that the Maleo would have a 1,200 cc engine and retail for an on-the-road cost of 25 million rupiah ($10,785).
Habibie clarified earlier reports that the Maleo would be a 1,600 cc car costing 20 million rupiah.
The reports in July said Habibie was considering using a motor developed by the Orbital Engine Corporation, but Antara did not say what engine the vehicle would use.

"We must have the benefit of local components which are the product of Indonesians. The Maleo national car will use 60 percent local components, while 40 percent will be overseas technology from Australia and the United Kingdom," Habibie said.

In February, Indonesia gave special tax and tariff breaks to PT Putra Timor Nasional to make a national car in partnership with Kia Motors of South Korea. The company is controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra.
The controversial move was attacked by Japan, Europe and the United States for violating World Trade Organisation rules.

The 1,600 cc Timor sedan enters the market next month at a price of 35 million rupiah, considerably cheaper than existing models, with the company initially selling fully built-up vehicles before beginning local assembly next March.
